title: Acceptance bound for an incorrect product
statement: Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$, and let a seed map each $r$-bit string to a vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. Suppose the density obtained by pushing the uniform seed distribution forward has every nonzero Fourier coefficient of absolute value at most $\varepsilon$, and suppose $C'\ne AB$. Then the seeded verification acceptance probability is at most $(1+\varepsilon)/2$.
hypotheses_covered: Matrices A, B, and C' over the two-element field
Seed map from r-bit strings to vectors in F₂ⁿ
All nonzero Fourier coefficients of the pushed-forward density have absolute value at most ε
C' is not equal to AB
